title: power-scenarios.json contract
description: Structural contract for asic/<module>/Verification/simulation-plan/power-scenarios.json — one entry per scenario materialized from references/power-scenarios-template.md's standard set. Read by power-analysis alone, and these four fields are exactly what it reads: it keys SAIF and PT-PX reports by id, groups runs by sequence_ref, drives the test's run length from duration_cycles, and annotates every power number with corner_intent. The standard set's abstract columns (clock / reset / data / low-power state, the scenario name, its purpose) are NOT here: no program reads them, so they belong in verification-plan.md §4 beside the per-scenario materialization note that explains them. sequence_ref resolving against sequences.json is not expressible here; the check-scaffold gate enforces it, where both files are in hand.

id.description: The standard set's scenario id (S1 … S7, or S8+ for a supplement). Every SAIF file and PT-PX report directory is named after it, and power-analysis's result.json keys its per-scenario rows by it.

sequence_ref.description: A sequences.json entry's name. emit_power_tests groups by this and runs each group once, so two scenarios that reduce to the same RTL stimulus share one value and stay distinct by id + corner_intent.

corner_intent.description: PVT corner this scenario is annotated at (e.g. "SS/125C"). RTL simulation is corner-agnostic, so this is the only place the corner is stated — power-analysis's result.schema.json requires it on every SAIF and every power row.
